title: Your own rules
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What rule have you set for your own team that someone else would call censorship?

Jose said that the social network has terms of service, and the right to suspend accounts on violation, and what counts as a violation is not concrete. It is interpreted in many ways. He said we should all go and read the terms, which are totally open to interpretation.

A student said: these are private businesses. In free-market capitalism I think private businesses should be able to do what they want, and it should be the people's choice whether to use a platform that they know censors. But I am being hypocritical, because it was already a massive part of the population.

Jose said that as leaders, as entrepreneurs, I believe you have to take a position, because we are what we listen to, what we read and what we write. Censorship can be as simple as saying in your company, as I'm guilty of: I don't want any negative comments.

It's all possibility thinking, no impossibility thinking, no negative comments, no victimization, he said. A student said: you're not taking away people's rights by doing that, because they have the right not to participate in this company.

Jose said: and if a government says that, you're saying they have the right to leave the country? A student said: I disagree with any system where you do not have the choice. Another said: there's a choice in every decision.
What position do you take, and what would you ask your team to say about it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the rules you set for your team about what can be said.
Write which of them someone could call censorship.
Write what you would say to a team member who disagrees.
Write the choice people have to leave.
Write your position, in two sentences.

check.q: What did Jose say you have to take as a leader?
What example of censorship in a company did Jose give about himself?
choices: Saying: I don't want any negative comments

check.q: What did a student say about private businesses?
choices: They should do what they want, and people can choose

recap: Take a position. Be honest about the rules you set in your own company.
